chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.مِثْلُهُ: Like it / The same (referring to a previous ruling or narration)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Like it' imply in the context of confession during illness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This is a *mutawatir*-style chain of transmission (isnad) within Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, linking the narration of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through a prominent chain of Kufan scholars, specifically highlighting the reliability of Dawud ibn al-Husayn. It confirms that the legal principles regarding confession (iqrar) during illness, particularly concerning the distribution of wealth or testimony, are firmly established in Imami jurisprudence. The brevity of the text underscores the consensus among the narrators regarding the applicability of the preceding ruling to the specific context of sickness.
